newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans larger wheat import tax rise.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans larger wheat import tax rise.

text.p: Turkey is planning a larger rise in the wheat import tax than the initial proposal to protect its farmers and divert wheat processors to local output, a senior farm official said on Thursday.
He told Reuters the government also planned a rise in the corn import tax, bringing forward a plan to raise the tax in October, when the corn crop comes out.
The present taxes on wheat and corn imports are 15 percent.
"Yes, the increase will go up further," said the official when asked whether the government would alter the proposed rise in the wheat import tax.
"I really cannot tell the new rates," he said.
But market sources, flour producers and grain traders said the original plan to raise the wheat import tax to 25 percent would be changed to 30-40 percent.
"The corn import rates will also be raised," the official said.
Traders said said the corn tax could go up to 25-30 percent.
The official said the decree governing the rises in wheat and corn imports was awaiting the approval of the outgoing coalition government.
"We cannot say when the decree will be approved, given the current government situation," he said.
Local traders said domestic wheat prices ranged between 28,000 lira per kg ($190.7 per tonne) and 33,000 lira, compared with world prices of about $160 per tonne.
"In view of the price difference between the world and Turkey, the government should impose a realistic tax to stop imports," said the official.
